Hotspot species boards

Each board lists the species reported from one Hammersmith & Fulham eBird hotspot in the selected month. Counts are species reports, not unique birds.

Arrivals & Departures

Understanding seasonal movements

Birds use the borough in different ways: some remain throughout the year, others visit for summer or winter, and some pass through on migration. Partial migrants combine resident and migratory populations; scarce or irregular records do not imply a predictable seasonal visit.

These patterns describe historical reporting, not live movements or a forecast. Arrival and departure timings below reflect recurring first- and last-record months in borough records; they do not prove when individual birds arrive or leave.

Contributor species boards

Each board lists the species reported by one publicly named eBird checklist observer in the selected month. Names are the public display names returned by eBird; the board does not show email or contact details. Nearby mapped-location records are excluded; counted-bird totals appear only where eBird supplies them.

Sources

The board brings together expected seasonal movements, reported borough sightings, historical species records and automated acoustic detections. A report confirms a submitted observation at a place and date; by itself, it does not prove a first arrival, departure or local breeding.

Expected movements: Arrival and departure months are based primarily on historical records from Hammersmith & Fulham. Typical timings are derived from recurring patterns observed across multiple years of borough records. Earliest and latest months show the historical range of occurrence. These timings are intended as seasonal guidance and are not forecasts. Local evidence takes precedence over national reference material where sufficient borough data exists.

BirdWeather detections: public BirdNET audio detections from listening stations whose coordinates fall inside the borough boundary. They are automated sound identifications, not human-verified sightings or individual-bird counts; confidence is a model score, not confirmation.

Actual sightings: valid reports from eBird hotspots and other mapped locations within Hammersmith & Fulham are refreshed daily. Nearby reports come from eBird’s recent geospatial feed, which returns recent records (the latest observation per species in its search area); coordinates are clipped to the borough boundary and private locations are omitted. The nearby feed supplements the hotspot checklist feed, which retains multiple reports per hotspot. These records are evidence of reports, not proof of first arrival, departure or local breeding.

Hotspot map: markers show public eBird hotspot locations inside the borough; private mapped locations are not plotted. Background map tiles are provided by OpenStreetMap and load from its servers when the map is opened. Species names link to the RSPB A–Z search.

Historical species list: species-level aggregates from the validated eBird borough archive and public species layer. Counts are archive records, not individual birds. Last recorded is the latest observation date in that archive; it is not updated by the recent-sightings API feed and is not a claim about the latest sighting anywhere in the borough. Coverage is incomplete and a missing record does not prove absence. Recent reports are shown separately under Local sightings.
